item.description:
What's new in 0.12.1

  • The Compass now opens the way it was designed: the app's context menu is up, the app launcher left, window actions right, and the universal menu down. If you had never rearranged it, yours follows; a hand-arranged Compass keeps your order

What's new in 0.12.0

  • The pill library learned your habits: the Suggestions tile (formerly "Clipboard") now also lists the shortcuts you actually press in the app that was in front when you opened the menu — newest first, named from the app's own menu bar with the keys beneath. Drag one onto a ring and it becomes a Switch + Shortcut pill for that app. Reflexes like ⌘C/⌘V, your own triggers and shortcuts already on a ring are left out
  • The Tray: collect pills while arranging and drop the copies into another menu. Opening the library always lands on the categories; pull down for the A-Z list, and the pill you drag rides above the library on its way out
  • Escape now backs out exactly one step: an open confirm, then a folder, then a sub-menu, then the menu — and inside an editor window it closes that window. Closing an editor with unsaved edits asks Save / Discard / Cancel; Cancel on an edit page really discards, the ring snaps back
  • The ✓/✕ confirm beside a pill inside a folder emerges from under its pill and retracts into it at the folder's own pace; it always sits above its neighbours, and backing out of it sounds like navigation, not a refusal
  • Editor windows open beside the ring — right of it, left if there's no room — and every page of the editor re-places itself there; the pointer no longer jumps when an editor opens or after cancelling a confirm
  • The little name/shortcut bubble on hover now sits on the line from the centre through the pill, for every pill
  • The "3D light" rim around the hub and pills is gone for good
  • Compass: the hub no longer leans toward the pointer; ↑/↓ select a pill, ←/→ switch between the universal menus; holding a navigation key no longer machine-guns; the menu closes with the same sound it opened with, and cancelling keeps its own sound
  • The pointer trail shows only while you're using the menu — never in arrange mode or under an editor
  • Right-clicking the hub: the gear now gives the same feedback as the pencil on a pill
  • Folder feel: a folder you close by pulling back stays closed until you step off the pill and come back; the goo strand no longer sticks out after a folder closes, and it stops short of coloured pills
  • Safeguards in the editor sit 2×2 with the undo seconds on their own row; the undo cancel target aims where the pill actually flew, inside folders too
  • Smoother openings: the menu is fully drawn before it appears (no half-drawn frames after long idles or on the first open after wake), and swapping between menus keeps the pills together with their bodies

What's new in 0.11.0

  • Report a bug from inside the app: menu bar icon → "Report a Bug…" — type what happened, hit send. Version, macOS and the recent app log travel along automatically; if the server is unreachable it falls back to an email so nothing is lost
  • Shortcut Map (menu bar → "Shortcut Map…"): see every keyboard shortcut your apps and macOS already claim, grouped per app with icons. Type a shortcut you're planning and it tells you instantly whether it's free, taken system-wide, or would override something inside an app — or just press shortcuts and watch it identify them live
  • New pill type: System — toggle Mute, Dark Mode, Wi-Fi, Play/Pause, a Focus, or lock the screen straight from the ring
  • New safeguard: "Click only" — a pill that only fires on a real click, so a swipe can never trigger it by accident
  • Macros grew up: steps can open or focus an app, run another pill, and carry an "only if app X is (or isn't) in front" condition — enough to build "focus Antinote, then press its shortcut" as one pill. Every pill type now explains itself when you hover over it in the editor
  • Folders finish their story: they hold up to 7 pills and say "Folder is full" when you try an 8th, show how many pills they carry on their face, dissolve when you drag the last pill out, and while you hover a drop you can already see which pill would get promoted
  • Hold W/A/S/D or an arrow key from any menu to aim at another menu, swipe, and release the key to fire — the keys now work as hold-and-release triggers everywhere, not just in the Compass
  • The buttons above arrange mode explain themselves on hover (with the proper pause before showing)
  • Opening the menu is smoother: the windows are built once and kept warm instead of being rebuilt, the first open after hours away no longer stutters, and the pointer no longer jumps when an edit panel opens
  • Moving a pill in arrange mode now always makes room: everything between slides over one seat — including linked pairs, which travel as one piece and can never be split apart by a slide. Hold ⇧ while dropping to trade places instead
  • Dropping a pill in arrange mode plays the same sound as triggering one, and every time your drag aims at a new seat you get the familiar hover tick
  • All wiggling pills rock in sync, and the pill in your hand keeps wiggling — including a grabbed ⌥ face
  • In the Compass, the arrow keys and W/A/S/D both work at the same time
  • The app picker now finds iPhone/iPad apps installed on your Mac (like WhatsApp), and you can drag any app from Finder straight onto the app box in the edit panel
